questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The founding and financing of the Liverpool and Manchester Railway
How stationary steam engines were built to haul coal and freight
The history, trial win, and preservation of the Rocket locomotive
The life and engineering career of George Stephenson
questions.explain: It covers Rocket's design, Rainhill win, later use and museum preservation.

questions.q: Who is credited with the multi-tube boiler suggestion?
options: Joseph Locke
George Stephenson
Henry Booth
Thomas Cochrane
questions.explain: Henry Booth, treasurer of the L&MR, is believed to have suggested a multi-tube boiler.

questions.q: How was Rocket transported from Newcastle to Liverpool for re-assembly before the trials?
options: First by horse wagon to Carlisle, then transported onwards to Liverpool for re-assembly
By horse wagon to Carlisle, then a lighter to Port Carlisle, and finally by the Cumberland steamer to Liverpool
Taken by canal to Manchester, then moved by horse wagon onward to Rainhill for re-assembly
Transported on road to Carlisle, then shipped by rail to Liverpool before being reassembled at Rainhill
questions.explain: Rocket was dismantled at Newcastle and taken by horse wagon to Carlisle, lighter to Port Carlisle and then by the Cumberland steamer to Liverpool for re-assembly.

questions.q: Who was killed by Rocket at the 1830 opening ceremony?
options: Robert Stephenson
The Duke of Wellington
William Huskisson
Joseph Locke
questions.explain: William Huskisson, MP for Liverpool, was struck and killed at Parkside.

questions.q: Why was Rocket designed light and fast with moderate hauling power?
options: Its builder had run short of iron and copper for the boiler
Passengers disliked riding behind heavy and slow engines
The trial's weight limits and emphasis on speed favored that
It was meant to haul long freight trains between mines
questions.explain: Stephenson realised the contest rules would favour a fast, light locomotive of only moderate hauling power.
